end.summary:
Discussed the meaning of food miles as the distance food travels in kilometres.
Compared local potatoes and Shimla apples using distance and a map.
Connected longer journeys with more fuel use, pollution, packaging, waste, and reduced freshness.
Teach-back was not completed successfully; two unaided attempts were recorded.
end.parentNote: Rohan practised defining food miles and comparing foods by their source and travel distance. They connected longer journeys with more fuel, pollution, packaging, waste, and less freshness. At first, they assumed the potatoes came from a nearby market, but this was not confirmed or corrected later in the lesson. At home, ask them to choose two foods and discuss which likely travelled farther and why.
